title: How to 'Dish Up' Something Good
credits: Anna Matteo wrote this story for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: And now, Words and Their Stories, from VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: 现在,我们来学习"词汇与他们的故事",来自美国之音英语学习。

sentences.en: Food is a popular subject with many people around the world.
sentences.zh: 食物是世界上许多人喜爱的话题。

sentences.en: It is fun to talk about our favorite dishes.
sentences.zh: 谈论我们最喜欢的菜肴是一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: It is even more fun to share a favorite dish with others.
sentences.zh: 与他人分享一道喜爱的菜肴更是乐趣无穷。

sentences.en: Today we talk about the word “dish.”
sentences.zh: 今天我们来聊聊"dish"这个词。

sentences.en: A dish can be the object on which you serve food.
sentences.zh: dish可以指你盛放食物的器皿。

sentences.en: But, a dish can also mean a specially prepared food.
sentences.zh: 但是,dish也可以指特别准备的食物。

sentences.en: Do you have a signature dish?
sentences.zh: 你有自己拿手的招牌菜吗?

sentences.en: Our signature is how we sign our names.
sentences.zh: 我们的签名就是我们签署名字的方式。

sentences.en: So, a signature dish is a dish we are known for making well.
sentences.zh: 所以,招牌菜就是我们擅长制作、为人所知的菜肴。

sentences.en: In a way, it identifies us.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上,它代表了我们的身份。

sentences.en: My signature dish is sweet potato rosemary dinner rolls.
sentences.zh: 我的招牌菜是红薯迷迭香晚餐卷。

sentences.en: I am often asked to make them, especially for holiday parties.
sentences.zh: 我常常被请来制作这些面包,尤其是在节日聚会上。

sentences.en: In my circle of friends, I am known for this dish.
sentences.zh: 在我的朋友圈里,我以这道菜而闻名。

sentences.en: When the rolls are on the table, people know that I made them.
sentences.zh: 当这些面包端上餐桌时,人们就知道是我做的。

sentences.en: A tasty dish is something that makes a table look good and inviting.
sentences.zh: 一道美味的菜肴能让餐桌显得美观而诱人。

sentences.en: Sometimes the same can be said about a person.
sentences.zh: 有时,这种情况也可以用来形容一个人。

sentences.en: Someone who is good-looking can be called a dish.
sentences.zh: 一个长得好看的人可以被称为"dish"。

sentences.en: While this usage might be a bit dated, it is still used.
sentences.zh: 虽然这种用法可能有些过时,但它仍然在使用。

sentences.en: Now, let’s talk about the verb “dish.”
sentences.zh: 现在,我们来聊聊动词"dish"。

sentences.en: “To dish” can mean to talk about private or personal information.
sentences.zh: “to dish”可以指谈论私密或个人信息。

sentences.en: It might be gossip.
sentences.zh: 那可能是八卦。

sentences.en: But I can also dish about myself.
sentences.zh: 但我也可以“dish”关于我自己的事。

sentences.en: For example, a friend may ask me to dish about my new job.
sentences.zh: 例如，朋友可能会让我讲讲我的新工作。

sentences.en: I could also use a phrasal verb form and say my friend want me to dish out all the interesting details.
sentences.zh: 我也可以改用短语动词形式，说我的朋友想让我把所有有趣的细节都抖出来。

sentences.en: Now, to dish up something means to put food on a dish for someone to eat.
sentences.zh: 现在，“to dish up something”指把食物盛到盘子里给别人吃。

sentences.en: However, it can also mean sharing personal details, our own and others.
sentences.zh: 不过，它也可以指分享个人信息，无论是自己的还是别人的。

sentences.en: We can also dish out things, like jokes or even insults.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以“dish out”一些东西，比如笑话甚至侮辱。

sentences.en: Some people like to tease or insult.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢取笑或侮辱别人。

sentences.en: They can dish out jokes and insults all day long.
sentences.zh: 他们可以一整天都讲笑话、出言侮辱。

sentences.en: But sometimes these same people do not like it if you do the same to them.
sentences.zh: 但有时这些人同样不喜欢你对他们这样做。

sentences.en: We have a saying for just such people.
sentences.zh: 对于这样的人，我们有一句俗语。

sentences.en: We say, “They can dish it out, but they can’t take it.”
sentences.zh: 我们说：“他们能往外面泼脏水，却受不了别人泼回来。”

sentences.en: They are able and willing to share harsh thoughts, criticisms, or insults about others, but they do not think they, themselves, deserve such treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们乐于且愿意分享对别人的刻薄之词、批评或侮辱，却不认为他们自己配得上这样的对待。

sentences.en: And that’s Words and Their Stories.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《词与故事》。

sentences.en: Until next time, I’m Anna Matteo.
sentences.zh: 下次见，我是安娜·马泰奥。

glossary.def: the name of a person written with his or her own hand
rumor or report of a personal nature
